extracted_claims.text: The AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the date Chapter III (high-risk system obligations, including Annex III) would start to apply, 36 months after entry into force.

The 'AI Omnibus' (Digital Omnibus on AI) was proposed by the Commission to delay application of high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months, making application conditional on confirmation that needed standards and tools are available.
The AI Omnibus legislative proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, a political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and it entered into force on 27 July 2026.
Following the AI Omnibus, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027.
The obligations for high-risk AI systems that are classified as high-risk because they are embedded in regulated products listed in Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) apply from 2 August 2028.

Article 113 of the consolidated AI Act text (as amended, version dated 27 July 2026) states that operators of high-risk AI systems placed on the market before the 'date of application of Chapter III' are only covered if subject to significant design changes after that date.
A news blog reports that under a 'final text agreed in September 2026,' the Annex III high-risk obligations were moved again to 2 August 2029, rather than 2 December 2027.
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with prohibitions and AI literacy obligations applying from 2 February 2025, and governance/GPAI obligations applying from 2 August 2025.

Transparency obligations under Article 50 enter into application and are enforceable from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for legacy systems to comply with marking/detection duties under Article 50(2).
New prohibitions relating to non-consensual sexual deepfakes and child sexual abuse material apply from 2 December 2026.

A May 2026 Council/Parliament press release describes the Commission's proposal (not yet finalized at that date) to adjust the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months, contingent on standards readiness confirmation.
Some commentary (pre-Omnibus or based on outdated information) continues to describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations.

Article 113 (pre-Omnibus text) stated the Regulation 'shall apply from 2 August 2026,' with Chapter III Sections 1-3 (high-risk rules) subject to that general application date, subject to limited exceptions.
Annex III itself lists eight categories of AI use cases that can be classified as high-risk; it is not a list of systems automatically deemed high-risk.

report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations, 36 months after the Act's entry into force (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). However, following adoption of the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI), which entered into force on 27 July 2026, the applicable date for Annex III high-risk obligations has been postponed to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
The AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the date Chapter III (high-risk system obligations, including Annex III) would start to apply, 36 months after entry into force (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). Separately, the Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with prohibitions and AI literacy obligations applying from 2 February 2025 and governance/GPAI obligations applying from 2 August 2025 (low confidence, as this detail is sourced primarily from lower-authority commentary) ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline), [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)). The pre-Omnibus Article 113 text stated the Regulation "shall apply from 2 August 2026," covering Chapter III Sections 1–3 (low confidence) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### The AI Omnibus and Revised Timeline
The Commission proposed the "Digital Omnibus on AI" to delay high-risk rules by up to 16 months, conditional on confirming the availability of necessary standards and conformity tools (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). The proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, with political agreement reached on 7 May 2026, and entry into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy — Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). As a result, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), a conclusion corroborated by numerous official EU and legal-analysis sources ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

### Related Deadlines
High-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) face a later deadline of **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Transparency obligations under Article 50 remain enforceable from 2 August 2026, with a transitional period until 2 December 2026 for legacy systems' marking/detection duties (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). New prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM apply from 2 December 2026 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). Grandfathering provisions under Article 113 indicate that operators placing high-risk systems on the market before the Chapter III application date are only covered if the system undergoes significant design changes afterward (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A news blog source claims the deadline was further delayed to 2 August 2029 under a "final text agreed in September 2026" — this is **unverified** and contradicted by the overwhelming majority of official EU sources confirming 2 December 2027; confidence in this claim is low (0.12) and it should be disregarded absent corroboration ([unverified blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). Several commentary sources continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, reflecting pre-Omnibus information now superseded (low confidence) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)). There is also tension between a 7 May 2026 press release describing the delay as a still-negotiated proposal and other sources stating the Omnibus had already been adopted by that date, suggesting overlapping legislative stages were reported near-simultaneously (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear which formal Regulation number codifies the AI Omnibus amendments and whether it matches the instrument entering into force on 27 July 2026. It is not confirmed whether the 2 December 2027 date remains conditional on standards-readiness confirmation, as originally proposed, or is now fixed. The reliability of the 2029 delay claim is unresolved. Whether all Annex III categories share the identical 2 December 2027 date, or whether sub-provisions (e.g., Article 6(2)) diverge, is not fully clarified across sources.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations, 36 months after the Act's entry into force (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). However, following adoption of the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI), which entered into force on 27 July 2026, the applicable date for Annex III high-risk obligations has been postponed to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with prohibitions and AI literacy obligations applying from 2 February 2025, governance and GPAI obligations from 2 August 2025, and Chapter III (including Annex III high-risk obligations) originally set to apply from 2 August 2026 (low confidence, given this claim is sourced from lower-authority commentary) ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). The pre-Omnibus Article 113 text stated the Regulation "shall apply from 2 August 2026," covering Chapter III Sections 1–3 (low confidence) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### The AI Omnibus and Revised Timeline
The Commission proposed the "Digital Omnibus on AI" to delay high-risk rules by up to 16 months, conditional on confirming the availability of necessary standards and conformity tools (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). The proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, with political agreement reached on 7 May 2026, and entry into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy — Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). As a result, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), a conclusion corroborated by numerous official EU and legal-analysis sources ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

### Related Deadlines
High-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) face a later deadline of **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Transparency obligations under Article 50 remain enforceable from 2 August 2026, with a transitional period until 2 December 2026 for legacy systems' marking/detection duties (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). New prohibitions on non-consensual sexual deepfakes and CSAM apply from 2 December 2026 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). Grandfathering provisions under Article 113 indicate that operators placing high-risk systems on the market before the Chapter III application date are only covered if the system undergoes significant design changes afterward (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A news blog source claims the deadline was further delayed to 2 August 2029 under a "final text agreed in September 2026" — this is **unverified** and contradicted by the overwhelming majority of official EU sources confirming 2 December 2027; confidence in this claim is low (0.12) and it should be disregarded absent corroboration ([unverified blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). Several commentary sources continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, reflecting pre-Omnibus information now superseded (low confidence) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)). There is also tension between a 7 May 2026 press release describing the delay as a still-negotiated proposal and other sources stating the Omnibus had already been adopted by that date, suggesting overlapping legislative stages were reported near-simultaneously (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear which formal Regulation number codifies the AI Omnibus amendments and whether it matches the instrument entering into force on 27 July 2026. It is not confirmed whether the 2 December 2027 date remains conditional on standards-readiness confirmation, as originally proposed, or is now fixed. The reliability of the 2029 delay claim is unresolved. Whether all Annex III categories share the identical 2 December 2027 date, or whether sub-provisions (e.g., Article 6(2)) diverge, is not fully clarified across sources.
